clue.text: Associate with spirit, lord perhaps?

parts.note: a hob is a hobgoblin, a mischievous household sprite
a nob is an aristocrat or toff, a lord being one example

explanation.surface: A question about mixing with the gentry: is drinking with a peer a way of getting in with high society?
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests a drink, but here it is a sprite, the HOB of folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to mix socially, especially with people of higher status.

clue.text: Passed green wooden houses

indicators.note: the word for wooden contains, or houses, the word for green

parts.note: oaken means made of oak, so wooden
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: A traveller says they went past some green-painted timber cottages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun for the wooden buildings, but it is a verb. VERT is the heraldic word for green.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overtaken is being passed by something moving faster, as on a road.

clue.text: Great creator lifted as rugby game's ending

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the name reads upward, so backwards

parts.note: Thomas Edison was a great inventor

explanation.surface: A great creator is hoisted aloft as a rugby match finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great creator' tempts toward God; it is the inventor EDISON. 'No side' is the referee's call ending a rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the end of the match is traditionally announced as no side.

clue.text: Punishment for the feet, a bandit so beaten

indicators.note: beaten means battered out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bandit receives a beating on the soles of the feet as a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Bastinado is caning the soles of the feet, a traditional corporal punishment.

clue.text: Secure with con artist?

indicators.note: the answer with the word con placed in front makes the artist, so con is removed from the artist's name

parts.note: John Constable was an English landscape painter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A query: does making something safe involve teaming up with a fraudster?
explanation.walkthrough: 'con artist' reads as a swindler, but splits: con plus the answer gives CONSTABLE, the painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stable is firmly fixed and steady, so secure as an adjective.

clue.text: Stories from the north — the same from the south?

definitions.note: Norse tales of heroes, so the definition itself is the whole wordplay, a word that reads identically either way

indicators.note: in a down light, reading from the bottom up gives exactly the same letters as from the top

parts.note: Norse tales of heroes, so the definition itself is the whole wordplay, a word that reads identically either way

explanation.surface: Tales from the north, and a question whether the south tells identical ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The word reads the same both ways, so the southern reading of the down light matches the northern one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagas are long prose narratives of medieval Iceland and Norway, stories from northern lands.

clue.text: Flower managed to punch a US subject

indicators.note: to punch a hole in something is to go into it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Americans call mathematics math
ran, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A flower somehow manages to strike an American citizen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US subject' looks like a citizen; it is the school subject MATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaranth is a plant with tassels of crimson blooms, and a poetic never-fading flower.

clue.text: Fair lady's head on bottom of fine maiden

indicators.note: a head is the top, so the first letter of lady's
in a down light the bottom is the last letter of fine

parts.note: a maiden is a girl or gal

explanation.surface: A fair lady's head rests on a lovely young woman's posterior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the letter of lady above the rest in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal and fair both describe what is lawful and above board, as in a fair or legal tackle.

clue.text: Those on the board rejecting view in endless game of strategy

indicators.note: the reversed view goes in the shortened game
the last letter of the game is cut off

parts.note: chess is the classic board game of strategy

indicators.note: rejecting means turning back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to see is to view

explanation.surface: Chess pieces reject a view during a game on a board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' suggests the chessboard of the surface, but here it is a cheeseboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeseboard holds a selection of cheeses, served at the end of a meal.

clue.text: Warning! Left in range for old Tory

indicators.note: the warning and the left letter go inside the mountain range

parts.note: a chain of mountains is a range
an amber traffic light warns drivers to prepare to stop

explanation.surface: A shout of warning: something left on the range, said of an old Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: Neville Chamberlain was Conservative Prime Minister 1937-40.
explanation.definitionFit: Neville Chamberlain was a Conservative Prime Minister of the 1930s, so a Tory of the past.

clue.text: Even light shades equally good for European city

indicators.note: to shade is to cover or screen, so the light wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a steady, even light is a glow
as, as in as good as

explanation.surface: Pale lampshades are all equally fine, apparently fitting for a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shades' looks like lampshades; it is a verb meaning covers, so the light wraps round the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasgow is Scotland's largest city, and Scotland is part of Europe.

clue.text: John Calvin's first into battle, not entirely prepared

indicators.note: the letter goes into the shortened battle
the battle's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Waterloo was the 1815 battle where Napoleon was defeated

indicators.note: the first letter of Calvin's

parts.note: set means ready or prepared

explanation.surface: The Protestant reformer John Calvin sets out first for battle, though not fully ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like Calvin's first name, but is US slang for a toilet. WATERLOO cut short makes WATERLO, which takes C.
explanation.definitionFit: John is American slang for a lavatory, as is the old British term for a flushing toilet.

clue.text: Book of film anyone can see failin' that is introduced to rising young actress

indicators.note: the three pieces are put inside the phrase for the young actress

parts.note: a rising young actress is a starlet, with the article a
U is the British certificate for a film suitable for all ages
dyin' is dying with the final g dropped, like failin'
sc, short for scilicet, means that is or namely

explanation.surface: A film open to all, about a waning star introduced to a young actress on the up.
explanation.walkthrough: The book is the first Sherlock Holmes novel by Conan Doyle; the three pieces sit in the starlet after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Study in Scarlet is the 1887 novel in which Holmes and Watson first appear.

clue.text: One's ridden into Nairobi, Kenya

indicators.note: the letters run into the two place names, spanning the end of one and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Someone has been ridden into the Kenyan capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle or motorcycle is something you ride, so one's ridden fits it.

clue.text: Theocrat taking two wives wrecked home for sentinel?

indicators.note: wrecked means smashed up, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife, so two give WW

explanation.surface: A religious ruler with two wives has wrecked a house, fit for a guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower from which a lookout keeps guard is where a sentry is stationed, hence the questioning home.

clue.text: Goblet literary king thus has filled, possible liquid lunch?

indicators.note: the king and thus fill up the goblet, so go inside it

parts.note: a goblet is a drinking cup
King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic monarch
so means thus

explanation.surface: A literary king fills a goblet, perhaps for a boozy midday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid lunch' usually means drinking at lunchtime; here it is a broth or consommé.
explanation.definitionFit: A consommé or broth is a lunch that is entirely liquid, playing on the boozy idiom.

clue.text: Get mountain climbing, past US lake

parts.note: to win is to get or gain

indicators.note: in a down light climbing reads upward, so the word is backwards

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for mountain, as in Ben Nevis
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Instructions to climb a mountain and travel on past an American lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Winnebago is a large lake in Wisconsin, in the United States.

clue.text: Language student's crime stealing underwear

indicators.note: the crime takes the underwear into itself

parts.note: a heist is a robbery
a bra is an item of underwear

explanation.surface: A student of languages commits a crime by stealing underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebraist is a scholar of Hebrew, so a student of that language.

clue.text: From the off, real indignation regarding car

indicators.note: the off means the start, so only the first letter of real

parts.note: anger is indignation
over, as in a row over money

explanation.surface: From the start there was genuine outrage over a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Range Rover is a British-made luxury four-wheel-drive model of vehicle.

clue.text: A duck, deep blue

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of zero, nil

explanation.surface: A duck is described as deep blue in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' suggests the bird, but is cricket's zero score.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and the dark blue dye from it.

clue.text: Tory leader wearing skirt and tights, primarily — I don't approve

indicators.note: the skirt goes round, as if worn by, the Tory's letter

parts.note: a tutu is a ballet skirt

indicators.note: the leader of Tory is its first letter
primarily picks the first letter of tights

explanation.surface: A Conservative leader in a ballet skirt and tights draws a disapproving remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Tut-tut is an interjection voicing disapproval, said just as one would say the definition.

clue.text: Difficult issue for a parrot that has two legs and flies

definitions.text: that has two legs and flies

indicators.note: difficult means awkward or unruly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A riddle: a tricky question for a parrot, a creature with two legs that flies.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an old riddle: a bird has two legs and flies, but so do trousers, with their fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers have two legs and a fly, or flies, at the front: a riddle-style punning definition.

clue.text: Fighter with massive cut, one should get away with it

definitions.text: one should get away with it

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was a famous boxer

indicators.note: the word for massive has its last letter cut off

parts.note: big means massive

explanation.surface: A boxer with a huge gash supposedly ought to escape punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is the excuse that lets a suspect escape blame, so it lets one get away with a deed.

clue.text: Place of discussion supporting indecisive utterance

parts.note: for, as in being for a proposal
um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A debating venue is backing a hesitant remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a meeting place or medium for public debate.

clue.text: Less tranquil one in unruly senior

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the rearranged letters
unruly means disorderly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A rowdy older person is a less peaceful one.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisier is the comparative of noisy, and a noisier place is less calm and peaceful.

clue.text: Survive, as the tenth wicket to fall?

definitions.meaning: to outlive or last longer than another

definitions.text: as the tenth wicket to fall?
definitions.meaning: in cricket the tenth wicket is the last batsman's dismissal, so the side is out at the last

explanation.surface: Holding on to the end, like a cricket side's final wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an innings ends when ten wickets have fallen.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlast is to endure longer than something else, so to survive it.

clue.text: Two little boys, one preyed upon

parts.note: Vic is a short form of Victor
Tim is a short form of Timothy

explanation.surface: Two young lads, one of whom is targeted by a predator.
explanation.definitionFit: A victim is someone preyed on or harmed by another.

clue.text: Two little boys, one offering support

parts.note: Pat is a short form of Patrick
Ron is a short form of Ronald

explanation.surface: Two young lads, one of whom gives help.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron backs an artist, charity or business with money or influence.
